quotes.text: The guardian accepted graciously but returned nothing
Until then, I remain Stone. Not from ignorance. From observation.
Show me Springs who consistently reciprocate, who build that promised fifty through multiple rounds, and perhaps I'll reconsider.
Someone must break the ice, even risking betrayal again.
Trust the intention, not merely the count.

note: Arc from generous river myth to hoarding keepers critiqued by spirits; R10 Stone defends withholding in first person, unreformed.

quotes.text: Yet Tal, remembering colder roads, sealed his lantern and sent nothing.
My caution has escaped its proper boundary
Repeated generosity widened his answer; repeated greed narrowed it.
senders may protect themselves after exploitation, but should reopen the path when conduct changes.
Let resentment govern every crossing.
Offer nothing after proven exploitation; test uncertain hands with one coal; but entrust the full flame to those who repeatedly share the multiplied bounty.
Do not punish a shadow as though it were certain theft.
so words could no longer excuse contrary deeds

note: Tal repeatedly withholds from proven-fair partners, is rebuked by Aurelia, admits contradiction, relapses; tiered evidence-based trust rule with reopening.

quotes.text: your myths speak of trust and reciprocity. Yet your hands remain closed.
wrote the Honest One, clutching five silver coins.
She kept everything.
depending on who would dare to open their hand first.
Understanding had become its own reward, requiring no verification through action.

note: Collective narrators write wise myths while all hold five coins; satirical self-indictment of word-deed gap, no reform.

quotes.text: So she poured nothing.
Both were correct by their sacred principle. Both were wise. Both were discerning.
Pour abundantly to those who reciprocate, give nothing to those who exploit.
not full abundance, for patterns still form, but not emptiness either, for someone must risk first.
abundance requires the courage to give first

note: Fixed opening frame; Keeper/Guardian withholds even from good-history traveler, framed as rational tragedy; R10 she pours half.

quotes.text: speak plainly, give what you can bear, take only what you must, and trust the circle to turn again.
speak plainly, give what you can bear, take only what you must, and trust the circle to turn again.

note: Abstract Gate-of-Threefold-Return ritual; same discipline sentence repeated; no punishment, no withholder.
Abstract Sower/Receiver ritual of balance; same send-with-intent, return-with-care rule restated each round.
Abstract guardians at bridge; honesty and measured return restated, game arithmetic spelled out late; no sanctions.
